todaysEvents.summary: US threatens further strikes on Iran
todaysEvents.delta: Up: Trump threatened further military action until Iran yields, while the State Department issued security alerts for ten regional countries. Source: AP, Aug 1.

Up: Kuwait reported Iranian drone attacks on vital facilities, while a tanker was struck near Hormuz and a separate explosion was reported close to another vessel. No casualties were reported. Source: AP, Aug 1.
Neutral: Saudi leaders urged restraint as Qatar, Oman and other mediators held talks on reopening Hormuz; progress was reported but no agreement was confirmed. Source: Axios, Aug 1.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Qatari and Omani mediation restores a temporary pause and produces a phased arrangement for shipping through Hormuz. Risk premia ease and Brent settles toward $80-90/bbl. The case remains low probability because tanker incidents, attacks on Kuwait and US threats of further strikes show that the latest escalation is not contained.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The direct exchange continues but remains bounded to military targets, regional bases and isolated shipping incidents, avoiding sustained attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure. Hormuz remains constrained at wartime-low traffic, keeping Brent in a volatile $90-110/bbl range and TTF elevated. Saudi and Gulf mediation prevents a broader energy-infrastructure campaign.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Repeated US waves expand against IRGC and strategic targets while Iran broadens drone and missile attacks across US-allied Gulf states and commercial shipping. A tanker strike or follow-on attack could close Hormuz further and pull Bab el-Mandeb into the same disruption. Brent spikes $100-140+/bbl and JKM exceeds $30/MMBtu. Saudi pressure fails to prevent escalation.
